theirs: And these [were] they which went up from Telmelah, Telharsa, Cherub, Addan, [and] Immer: but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel:

ours: They gave after their ability unto the treasure of the work threescore and one thousand drams of gold, and five thousand pound of silver, and one hundred priests garments.
theirs: They gave after their ability unto the treasure of the work threescore and one thousand drams of gold, and five thousand pound of silver, and one hundred priests' garments.

ours: Then they came to Zerubbabel, and to the chief of the fathers, and said unto them, Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do; and we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar-haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.
theirs: Then they came to Zerubbabel, and to the chief of the fathers, and said unto them, Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye [do]; and we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.

ours: Now because we have maintenance from the kings palace, and it was not meet for us to see the kings dishonour, therefore have we sent and certified the king;
theirs: Now because we have maintenance from [the king's] palace, and it was not meet for us to see the king's dishonour, therefore have we sent and certified the king;

ours: Now when the copy of king Artaxerxes letter was read before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went up in haste to Jerusalem unto the Jews, and made them to cease by force and power.
theirs: Now when the copy of king Artaxerxes' letter [was] read before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went up in haste to Jerusalem unto the Jews, and made them to cease by force and power.

ours: At the same time came to them Tatnai, governor on this side the river, and Shethar-boznai, and their companions, and said thus unto them, Who hath commanded you to build this house, and to make up this wall?
theirs: At the same time came to them Tatnai, governor on this side the river, and Shetharboznai, and their companions, and said thus unto them, Who hath commanded you to build this house, and to make up this wall?

ours: The copy of the letter that Tatnai, governor on this side the river, and Shethar-boznai, and his companions the Apharsachites, which were on this side the river, sent unto Darius the king:
theirs: The copy of the letter that Tatnai, governor on this side the river, and Shetharboznai, and his companions the Apharsachites, which [were] on this side the river, sent unto Darius the king:

ours: Now therefore, if it seem good to the king, let there be search made in the kings treasure house, which is there at Babylon, whether it be so, that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem, and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.
theirs: Now therefore, if [it seem] good to the king, let there be search made in the king's treasure house, which [is] there at Babylon, whether it be [so], that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem, and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.

ours: With three rows of great stones, and a row of new timber: and let the expences be given out of the kings house:
theirs: [With] three rows of great stones, and a row of new timber: and let the expences be given out of the king's house:

ours: Now therefore, Tatnai, governor beyond the river, Shethar-boznai, and your companions the Apharsachites, which are beyond the river, be ye far from thence:
theirs: Now [therefore], Tatnai, governor beyond the river, Shetharboznai, and your companions the Apharsachites, which [are] beyond the river, be ye far from thence:

ours: Moreover I make a decree what ye shall do to the elders of these Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the kings goods, even of the tribute beyond the river, forthwith expences be given unto these men, that they be not hindered.
theirs: Moreover I make a decree what ye shall do to the elders of these Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king's goods, [even] of the tribute beyond the river, forthwith expences be given unto these men, that they be not hindered.

ours: Then Tatnai, governor on this side the river, Shethar-boznai, and their companions, according to that which Darius the king had sent, so they did speedily.
theirs: Then Tatnai, governor on this side the river, Shetharboznai, and their companions, according to that which Darius the king had sent, so they did speedily.

ours: And whatsoever more shall be needful for the house of thy God, which thou shalt have occasion to bestow, bestow it out of the kings treasure house.
theirs: And whatsoever more shall be needful for the house of thy God, which thou shalt have occasion to bestow, bestow [it] out of the king's treasure house.

ours: Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the kings heart, to beautify the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem:
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD God of our fathers, which hath put [such a thing] as this in the king's heart, to beautify the house of the LORD which [is] in Jerusalem:

ours: And hath extended mercy unto me before the king, and his counsellers, and before all the kings mighty princes. And I was strengthened as the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, and I gathered together out of Israel chief men to go up with me.
theirs: And hath extended mercy unto me before the king, and his counsellers, and before all the king's mighty princes. And I was strengthened as the hand of the LORD my God [was] upon me, and I gathered together out of Israel chief men to go up with me.

ours: Of the sons of Pahath-moab; Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males.
theirs: Of the sons of Pahathmoab; Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males.

ours: And they delivered the kings commissions unto the kings lieutenants, and to the governors on this side the river: and they furthered the people, and the house of God.
theirs: And they delivered the king's commissions unto the king's lieutenants, and to the governors on this side the river: and they furthered the people, and the house of God.

ours: And of the sons of Pahath-moab; Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.
theirs: And of the sons of Pahathmoab; Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.

ours: Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my fathers house have sinned.
theirs: Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my father's house have sinned.

ours: O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the kings cupbearer.
theirs: O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king's cupbearer.

ours: And said unto the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?
theirs: And said unto the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, [lieth] waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?

ours: And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers sepulchres, that I may build it.
theirs: And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers' sepulchres, that I may build it.

ours: And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the kings forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
theirs: And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which [appertained] to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.

ours: Then I came to the governors beyond the river, and gave them the kings letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.
theirs: Then I came to the governors beyond the river, and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.

ours: Then I went on to the gate of the fountain, and to the kings pool: but there was no place for the beast that was under me to pass.
theirs: Then I went on to the gate of the fountain, and to the king's pool: but [there was] no place for the beast [that was] under me to pass.

ours: Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the kings words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
theirs: Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king's words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for [this] good [work].

ours: Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hashub the son of Pahath-moab, repaired the other piece, and the tower of the furnaces.
theirs: Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hashub the son of Pahathmoab, repaired the other piece, and the tower of the furnaces.

ours: But the dung gate repaired Malchiah the son of Rechab, the ruler of part of Beth-haccerem; he built it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.
theirs: But the dung gate repaired Malchiah the son of Rechab, the ruler of part of Bethhaccerem; he built it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.

ours: But the gate of the fountain repaired Shallun the son of Col-hozeh, the ruler of part of Mizpah; he built it, and covered it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof, and the wall of the pool of Siloah by the kings garden, and unto the stairs that go down from the city of David.
theirs: But the gate of the fountain repaired Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of part of Mizpah; he built it, and covered it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof, and the wall of the pool of Siloah by the king's garden, and unto the stairs that go down from the city of David.

ours: After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the half part of Beth-zur, unto the place over against the sepulchres of David, and to the pool that was made, and unto the house of the mighty.
theirs: After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the half part of Bethzur, unto [the place] over against the sepulchres of David, and to the pool that was made, and unto the house of the mighty.

ours: Palal the son of Uzai, over against the turning of the wall, and the tower which lieth out from the kings high house, that was by the court of the prison. After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh.
theirs: Palal the son of Uzai, over against the turning [of the wall], and the tower which lieth out from the king's high house, that [was] by the court of the prison. After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh.

ours: After him repaired Malchiah the goldsmiths son unto the place of the Nethinims, and of the merchants, over against the gate Miphkad, and to the going up of the corner.
theirs: After him repaired Malchiah the goldsmith's son unto the place of the Nethinims, and of the merchants, over against the gate Miphkad, and to the going up of the corner.

ours: There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the kings tribute, and that upon our lands and vineyards.
theirs: There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king's tribute, [and that upon] our lands and vineyards.

ours: The children of Pahath-moab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand and eight hundred and eighteen.
theirs: The children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand and eight hundred [and] eighteen.

ours: The men of Beth-lehem and Netophah, an hundred fourscore and eight.
theirs: The men of Bethlehem and Netophah, an hundred fourscore and eight.

ours: The men of Beth-azmaveth, forty and two.
theirs: The men of Bethazmaveth, forty and two.

ours: The men of Kirjath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty and three.
theirs: The men of Kirjathjearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty and three.

ours: The men of Beth-el and Ai, an hundred twenty and three.
theirs: The men of Bethel and Ai, an hundred twenty and three.

ours: The children of Solomons servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Perida,
theirs: The children of Solomon's servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Perida,

ours: All the Nethinims, and the children of Solomons servants, were three hundred ninety and two.
theirs: All the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants, [were] three hundred ninety and two.

ours: And these were they which went up also from Tel-melah, Tel-haresha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer: but they could not shew their fathers house, nor their seed, whether they were of Israel.
theirs: And these [were] they which went up [also] from Telmelah, Telharesha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer: but they could not shew their father's house, nor their seed, whether they [were] of Israel.

ours: And some of the chief of the fathers gave unto the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasure a thousand drams of gold, fifty basons, five hundred and thirty priests garments.
theirs: And some of the chief of the fathers gave unto the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasure a thousand drams of gold, fifty basons, five hundred and thirty priests' garments.

ours: And that which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand drams of gold, and two thousand pound of silver, and threescore and seven priests garments.
theirs: And [that] which the rest of the people gave [was] twenty thousand drams of gold, and two thousand pound of silver, and threescore and seven priests' garments.

ours: Nevertheless for thy great mercies sake thou didst not utterly consume them, nor forsake them; for thou art a gracious and merciful God.
theirs: Nevertheless for thy great mercies' sake thou didst not utterly consume them, nor forsake them; for thou [art] a gracious and merciful God.

ours: The chief of the people; Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zatthu, Bani,
theirs: The chief of the people; Parosh, Pahathmoab, Elam, Zatthu, Bani,

ours: They clave to their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in Gods law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and his judgments and his statutes;
theirs: They clave to their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in God's law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and his judgments and his statutes;

ours: Now these are the chief of the province that dwelt in Jerusalem: but in the cities of Judah dwelt every one in his possession in their cities, to wit, Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nethinims, and the children of Solomons servants.
theirs: Now these [are] the chief of the province that dwelt in Jerusalem: but in the cities of Judah dwelt every one in his possession in their cities, [to wit], Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants.

ours: And Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni.
theirs: And Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Colhozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni.

ours: For it was the kings commandment concerning them, that a certain portion should be for the singers, due for every day.
theirs: For [it was] the king's commandment concerning them, that a certain portion should be for the singers, due for every day.

ours: And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabeel, of the children of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the kings hand in all matters concerning the people.
theirs: And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabeel, of the children of Zerah the son of Judah, [was] at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people.

ours: And for the villages, with their fields, some of the children of Judah dwelt at Kirjath-arba, and in the villages thereof, and at Dibon, and in the villages thereof, and at Jekabzeel, and in the villages thereof,
theirs: And for the villages, with their fields, [some] of the children of Judah dwelt at Kirjatharba, and [in] the villages thereof, and at Dibon, and [in] the villages thereof, and at Jekabzeel, and [in] the villages thereof,

ours: And at Jeshua, and at Moladah, and at Beth-phelet,
theirs: And at Jeshua, and at Moladah, and at Bethphelet,

ours: And at Hazar-shual, and at Beer-sheba, and in the villages thereof,
theirs: And at Hazarshual, and at Beersheba, and [in] the villages thereof,

ours: And at En-rimmon, and at Zareah, and at Jarmuth,
theirs: And at Enrimmon, and at Zareah, and at Jarmuth,

ours: Zanoah, Adullam, and in their villages, at Lachish, and the fields thereof, at Azekah, and in the villages thereof. And they dwelt from Beer-sheba unto the valley of Hinnom.
theirs: Zanoah, Adullam, and [in] their villages, at Lachish, and the fields thereof, at Azekah, and [in] the villages thereof. And they dwelt from Beersheba unto the valley of Hinnom.

ours: The children also of Benjamin from Geba dwelt at Michmash, and Aija, and Beth-el, and in their villages,
theirs: The children also of Benjamin from Geba [dwelt] at Michmash, and Aija, and Bethel, and [in] their villages,

ours: And certain of the priests sons with trumpets; namely, Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Michaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph:
theirs: And [certain] of the priests' sons with trumpets; [namely], Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Michaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph:

ours: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews language, but according to the language of each people.
theirs: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people.

ours: And when these days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the kings palace;
theirs: And when these days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king's palace;

ours: And the drinking was according to the law; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every mans pleasure.
theirs: And the drinking [was] according to the law; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every man's pleasure.

ours: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the kings commandment by his chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.
theirs: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by [his] chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.

ours: Then the king said to the wise men, which knew the times, (for so was the kings manner toward all that knew law and judgment:
theirs: Then the king said to the wise men, which knew the times, (for so [was] the king's manner toward all that knew law and judgment:

ours: And the next unto him was Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, which saw the kings face, and which sat the first in the kingdom;)
theirs: And the next unto him [was] Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, [and] Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, which saw the king's face, [and] which sat the first in the kingdom;)

ours: Likewise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the kings princes, which have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus shall there arise too much contempt and wrath.
theirs: [Likewise] shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the king's princes, which have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus [shall there arise] too much contempt and wrath.

ours: And when the kings decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.
theirs: And when the king's decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.

ours: For he sent letters into all the kings provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that it should be published according to the language of every people.
theirs: For he sent letters into all the king's provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that [it] should be published according to the language of every people.

ours: Then said the kings servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:
theirs: Then said the king's servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:

ours: And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody of Hege the kings chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given them:
theirs: And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody of Hege the king's chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given [them]:

ours: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncles daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.
theirs: And he brought up Hadassah, that [is], Esther, his uncle's daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid [was] fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.

ours: So it came to pass, when the kings commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the kings house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.
theirs: So it came to pass, when the king's commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the king's house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.

ours: And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens, which were meet to be given her, out of the kings house: and he preferred her and her maids unto the best place of the house of the women.
theirs: And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens, [which were] meet to be given her, out of the king's house: and he preferred her and her maids unto the best [place] of the house of the women.

ours: And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the womens house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.
theirs: And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women's house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.

ours: Now when every maids turn was come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that she had been twelve months, according to the manner of the women, (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished, to wit, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odours, and with other things for the purifying of the women;)
theirs: Now when every maid's turn was come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that she had been twelve months, according to the manner of the women, (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished, [to wit], six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odours, and with [other] things for the purifying of the women;)

ours: Then thus came every maiden unto the king; whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the kings house.
theirs: Then thus came [every] maiden unto the king; whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the king's house.

ours: In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the kings chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called by name.
theirs: In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king's chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called by name.

ours: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the kings chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
theirs: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.

ours: Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, even Esthers feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.
theirs: Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, [even] Esther's feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.

ours: And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the kings gate.
theirs: And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king's gate.

ours: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the kings gate, two of the kings chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
theirs: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.

ours: And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecais name.
theirs: And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told [it] unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king [thereof] in Mordecai's name.

ours: And all the kings servants, that were in the kings gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.
theirs: And all the king's servants, that [were] in the king's gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did [him] reverence.

ours: Then the kings servants, which were in the kings gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the kings commandment?
theirs: Then the king's servants, which [were] in the king's gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king's commandment?

ours: Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecais matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew.
theirs: Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's matters would stand: for he had told them that he [was] a Jew.

ours: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the kings laws: therefore it is not for the kings profit to suffer them.
theirs: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws [are] diverse from all people; neither keep they the king's laws: therefore it [is] not for the king's profit to suffer them.

ours: If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring it into the kings treasuries.
theirs: If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring [it] into the king's treasuries.

ours: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews enemy.
theirs: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews' enemy.

ours: Then were the kings scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded unto the kings lieutenants, and to the governors that were over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the kings ring.
theirs: Then were the king's scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded unto the king's lieutenants, and to the governors that [were] over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the writing thereof, and [to] every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the king's ring.

ours: And the letters were sent by posts into all the kings provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.
theirs: And the letters were sent by posts into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, [even] upon the thirteenth [day] of the twelfth month, which [is] the month Adar, and [to take] the spoil of them for a prey.

ours: The posts went out, being hastened by the kings commandment, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.
theirs: The posts went out, being hastened by the king's commandment, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.

ours: And came even before the kings gate: for none might enter into the kings gate clothed with sackcloth.
theirs: And came even before the king's gate: for none [might] enter into the king's gate clothed with sackcloth.

ours: And in every province, whithersoever the kings commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
theirs: And in every province, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, [there was] great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

ours: So Esthers maids and her chamberlains came and told it her. Then was the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him: but he received it not.
theirs: So Esther's maids and her chamberlains came and told [it] her. Then was the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him: but he received [it] not.

ours: Then called Esther for Hatach, one of the kings chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a commandment to Mordecai, to know what it was, and why it was.
theirs: Then called Esther for Hatach, [one] of the king's chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a commandment to Mordecai, to know what it [was], and why it [was].

ours: So Hatach went forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which was before the kings gate.
theirs: So Hatach went forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which [was] before the king's gate.

ours: And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the kings treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.
theirs: And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.

ours: All the kings servants, and the people of the kings provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
theirs: All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, [there is] one law of his to put [him] to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.

ours: And they told to Mordecai Esthers words.
theirs: And they told to Mordecai Esther's words.

ours: Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the kings house, more than all the Jews.
theirs: Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews.

ours: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy fathers house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
theirs: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, [then] shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for [such] a time as this?

ours: NOW it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on her royal apparel, and stood in the inner court of the kings house, over against the kings house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.
theirs: Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on [her] royal [apparel], and stood in the inner court of the king's house, over against the king's house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.

ours: Then went Haman forth that day joyful and with a glad heart: but when Haman saw Mordecai in the kings gate, that he stood not up, nor moved for him, he was full of indignation against Mordecai.
theirs: Then went Haman forth that day joyful and with a glad heart: but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king's gate, that he stood not up, nor moved for him, he was full of indignation against Mordecai.

ours: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the kings gate.
theirs: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.

ours: And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the kings chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
theirs: And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.

ours: And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this? Then said the kings servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.
theirs: And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this? Then said the king's servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.

ours: And the king said, Who is in the court? Now Haman was come into the outward court of the kings house, to speak unto the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
theirs: And the king said, Who [is] in the court? Now Haman was come into the outward court of the king's house, to speak unto the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.

ours: And the kings servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.
theirs: And the king's servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.

ours: And let this apparel and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the kings most noble princes, that they may array the man withal whom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.
theirs: And let this apparel and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king's most noble princes, that they may array the man [withal] whom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.

ours: Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, and take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, that sitteth at the kings gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.
theirs: Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, [and] take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, that sitteth at the king's gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.

ours: And Mordecai came again to the kings gate. But Haman hasted to his house mourning, and having his head covered.
theirs: And Mordecai came again to the king's gate. But Haman hasted to his house mourning, and having his head covered.

ours: And while they were yet talking with him, came the kings chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.
theirs: And while they [were] yet talking with him, came the king's chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.

ours: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the kings damage.
theirs: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king's damage.

ours: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the kings mouth, they covered Hamans face.
theirs: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther [was]. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

ours: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the kings wrath pacified.
theirs: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified.

ours: ON that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.
theirs: On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews' enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he [was] unto her.

ours: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the kings provinces:
theirs: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing [seem] right before the king, and I [be] pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which [are] in all the king's provinces:

ours: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the kings name, and seal it with the kings ring: for the writing which is written in the kings name, and sealed with the kings ring, may no man reverse.
theirs: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king's name, and seal [it] with the king's ring: for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may no man reverse.

ours: Then were the kings scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.
theirs: Then were the king's scribes called at that time in the third month, that [is], the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth [day] thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which [are] from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.

ours: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus name, and sealed it with the kings ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, and riders on mules, camels, and young dromedaries:
theirs: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus' name, and sealed [it] with the king's ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, [and] riders on mules, camels, [and] young dromedaries:

ours: So the posts that rode upon mules and camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the kings commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.
theirs: [So] the posts that rode upon mules [and] camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.

ours: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the kings commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.
theirs: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.

ours: NOW in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the kings commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)
theirs: Now in the twelfth month, that [is], the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)

ours: For Mordecai was great in the kings house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.
theirs: For Mordecai [was] great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.

ours: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the kings provinces? now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done.
theirs: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? now what [is] thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what [is] thy request further? and it shall be done.

ours: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which are in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this days decree, and let Hamans ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.
theirs: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which [are] in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.

ours: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Hamans ten sons.
theirs: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons.

ours: But the other Jews that were in the kings provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,
theirs: But the other Jews that [were] in the king's provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

ours: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brothers house:
theirs: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters [were] eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:

ours: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brothers house:
theirs: While he [was] yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters [were] eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:

ours: And said, Naked came I out of my mothers womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
theirs: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

ours: Now when Jobs three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
theirs: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

ours: Because it shut not up the doors of my mothers womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.
theirs: Because it shut not up the doors of my [mother's] womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

ours: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lions whelps are scattered abroad.
theirs: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.

ours: Or, Deliver me from the enemys hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?
theirs: Or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

ours: My days are swifter than a weavers shuttle, and are spent without hope.
theirs: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

ours: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrites hope shall perish:
theirs: So [are] the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish:

ours: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spiders web.
theirs: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust [shall be] a spider's web.

ours: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as mans days,
theirs: [Are] thy days as the days of man? [are] thy years as man's days,

ours: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild asss colt.
theirs: For vain man would be wise, though man be born [like] a wild ass's colt.

ours: I also could speak as ye do: if your soul were in my souls stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.
theirs: I also could speak as ye [do]: if your soul were in my soul's stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.

ours: My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the childrens sake of mine own body.
theirs: My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children's [sake] of mine own body.

ours: He shall suck the poison of asps: the vipers tongue shall slay him.
theirs: He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper's tongue shall slay him.

ours: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widows ox for a pledge.
theirs: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow's ox for a pledge.

ours: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vultures eye hath not seen:
theirs: [There is] a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture's eye hath not seen:

ours: The lions whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
theirs: The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.

ours: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widows heart to sing for joy.
theirs: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

ours: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbours door;
theirs: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or [if] I have laid wait at my neighbour's door;

ours: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mothers womb;)
theirs: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as [with] a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;)

ours: Let me not, I pray you, accept any mans person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.
theirs: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

ours: Behold, I am according to thy wish in Gods stead: I also am formed out of the clay.
theirs: Behold, I [am] according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

ours: His flesh shall be fresher than a childs: he shall return to the days of his youth:
theirs: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth:

ours: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than Gods?
theirs: Thinkest thou this to be right, [that] thou saidst, My righteousness [is] more than God's?

ours: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on Gods behalf.
theirs: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that [I have] yet to speak on God's behalf.

ours: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
theirs: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch.

ours: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons sons, even four generations.
theirs: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, [even] four generations.

ours: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potters vessel.
theirs: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.

ours: LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.>> LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many [are] they that rise up against me.

ours: HEAR me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David.>> Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me [when I was] in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.

ours: GIVE ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Nehiloth, A Psalm of David.>> Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.

ours: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

ours: Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies sake.
theirs: Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake.

ours: O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:
theirs: <<Shiggaion of David, which he sang unto the LORD, concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.>> O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:

ours: O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

ours: I WILL praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Muthlabben, A Psalm of David.>> I will praise [thee], O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.

ours: For the wicked boasteth of his hearts desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the LORD abhorreth.
theirs: For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, [whom] the LORD abhorreth.

ours: IN the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee as a bird to your mountain?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> In the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee [as] a bird to your mountain?

ours: The LORD is in his holy temple, the LORDs throne is in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.
theirs: The LORD [is] in his holy temple, the LORD's throne [is] in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.

ours: HELP, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.

ours: HOW long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?

ours: THE fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, [there is] none that doeth good.

ours: LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?

ours: PRESERVE me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.
theirs: <<Michtam of David.>> Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.

ours: HEAR the right, O LORD, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, that goeth not out of feigned lips.
theirs: <<A Prayer of David.>> Hear the right, O LORD, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, [that goeth] not out of feigned lips.

ours: I WILL love thee, O LORD, my strength.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David, the servant of the LORD, who spake unto the LORD the words of this song in the day [that] the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul: And he said,>> I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.

ours: He maketh my feet like hinds feet, and setteth me upon my high places.
theirs: He maketh my feet like hinds' [feet], and setteth me upon my high places.

ours: THE heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

ours: THE LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;

ours: THE king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!

ours: Thou hast given him his hearts desire, and hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah.
theirs: Thou hast given him his heart's desire, and hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah.

ours: MY God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Aijeleth Shahar, A Psalm of David.>> My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? [why art thou so] far from helping me, [and from] the words of my roaring?

ours: But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mothers breasts.
theirs: But thou [art] he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope [when I was] upon my mother's breasts.

ours: I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mothers belly.
theirs: I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou [art] my God from my mother's belly.

ours: Save me from the lions mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns.
theirs: Save me from the lion's mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns.

ours: For the kingdom is the LORDs: and he is the governor among the nations.
theirs: For the kingdom [is] the LORD's: and he [is] the governor among the nations.

ours: THE LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The LORD [is] my shepherd; I shall not want.

ours: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his names sake.
theirs: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.

ours: THE earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The earth [is] the LORD's, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

ours: UNTO thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.

ours: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness sake, O LORD.
theirs: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness' sake, O LORD.

ours: For thy names sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it is great.
theirs: For thy name's sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it [is] great.

ours: JUDGE me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; therefore I shall not slide.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; [therefore] I shall not slide.

ours: THE LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> The LORD [is] my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD [is] the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

ours: UNTO thee will I cry, O LORD my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Unto thee will I cry, O LORD my rock; be not silent to me: lest, [if] thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

ours: GIVE unto the LORD, O ye mighty, give unto the LORD glory and strength.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> Give unto the LORD, O ye mighty, give unto the LORD glory and strength.

ours: I WILL extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.
theirs: <<A Psalm [and] Song [at] the dedication of the house of David.>> I will extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.

ours: IN thee, O LORD, do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness.

ours: For thou art my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy names sake lead me, and guide me.
theirs: For thou [art] my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy name's sake lead me, and guide me.

ours: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me for thy mercies sake.
theirs: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me for thy mercies' sake.

ours: BLESSED is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David, Maschil.>> Blessed [is he whose] transgression [is] forgiven, [whose] sin [is] covered.

ours: I WILL bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David, when he changed his behaviour before Abimelech; who drove him away, and he departed.>> I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise [shall] continually [be] in my mouth.

ours: PLEAD my cause, O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Plead [my cause], O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.

ours: THE transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, that there is no fear of God before his eyes.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David the servant of the LORD.>> The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, [that there is] no fear of God before his eyes.

ours: FRET not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.

ours: O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

ours: I SAID, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [even] to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David.>> I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.

ours: I WAITED patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.

ours: BLESSED is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Blessed [is] he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.

ours: AS the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Maschil, for the sons of Korah.>> As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.

ours: WE have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, Maschil.>> We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, [what] work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.

ours: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies sake.
theirs: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.

ours: MY heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, for the sons of Korah, Maschil, A Song of loves.>> My heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue [is] the pen of a ready writer.

ours: Thine arrows are sharp in the heart of the kings enemies; whereby the people fall under thee.
theirs: Thine arrows [are] sharp in the heart of the king's enemies; [whereby] the people fall under thee.

ours: Kings daughters were among thy honourable women: upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.
theirs: Kings' daughters [were] among thy honourable women: upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.

ours: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy fathers house;
theirs: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father's house;

ours: The kings daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold.
theirs: The king's daughter [is] all glorious within: her clothing [is] of wrought gold.

ours: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the kings palace.
theirs: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king's palace.

ours: GOD is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth.>> God [is] our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

ours: O CLAP your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.

ours: GREAT is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.
theirs: <<A Song [and] Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> Great [is] the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, [in] the mountain of his holiness.

ours: HEAR this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> Hear this, all [ye] people; give ear, all [ye] inhabitants of the world:

ours: THE mighty God, even the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> The mighty God, [even] the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.

ours: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mothers son.
theirs: Thou sittest [and] speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother's son.

ours: HAVE mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.>> Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

ours: WHY boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech.>> Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God [endureth] continually.

ours: THE fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Mahalath, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: [there is] none that doeth good.

ours: SAVE me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David, when the Ziphims came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us?>> Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.

ours: GIVE ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David.>> Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.

ours: BE merciful unto me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Jonathelemrechokim, Michtam of David, when the Philistines took him in Gath.>> Be merciful unto me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.

ours: BE merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David, when he fled from Saul in the cave.>> Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until [these] calamities be overpast.

ours: DO ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David.>> Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?

ours: DELIVER me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him.>> Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.

ours: O GOD, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shushaneduth, Michtam of David, to teach; when he strove with Aramnaharaim and with Aramzobah, when Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the valley of salt twelve thousand.>> O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.

ours: HEAR my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Neginah, [A Psalm] of David.>> Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.

ours: Thou wilt prolong the kings life: and his years as many generations.
theirs: Thou wilt prolong the king's life: [and] his years as many generations.

ours: TRULY my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David.>> Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him [cometh] my salvation.

ours: O GOD, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.>> O God, thou [art] my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;

ours: HEAR my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

ours: PRAISE waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm [and] Song of David.>> Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.

ours: MAKE a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Song [or] Psalm.>> Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:

ours: GOD be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm [or] Song.>> God be merciful unto us, and bless us; [and] cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.

ours: LET God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm [or] Song of David.>> Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.

ours: SAVE me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, [A Psalm] of David.>> Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto [my] soul.

ours: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mothers children.
theirs: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mother's children.

ours: MAKE haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David, to bring to remembrance.>> [Make haste], O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.

ours: By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mothers bowels: my praise shall be continually of thee.
theirs: By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mother's bowels: my praise [shall be] continually of thee.

ours: GIVE the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] for Solomon.>> Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.

ours: TRULY God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> Truly God [is] good to Israel, [even] to such as are of a clean heart.

ours: O GOD, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
theirs: <<Maschil of Asaph.>> O God, why hast thou cast [us] off for ever? [why] doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?

ours: UNTO thee, O God, do we give thanks, unto thee do we give thanks: for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, A Psalm [or] Song of Asaph.>> Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks, [unto thee] do we give thanks: for [that] thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.

ours: IN Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm [or] Song of Asaph.>> In Judah [is] God known: his name [is] great in Israel.

ours: I CRIED unto God with my voice, even unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of Asaph.>> I cried unto God with my voice, [even] unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.

ours: GIVE ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
theirs: <<Maschil of Asaph.>> Give ear, O my people, [to] my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

ours: Man did eat angels food: he sent them meat to the full.
theirs: Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full.

ours: And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemys hand.
theirs: And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemy's hand.

ours: O GOD, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.

ours: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name: and deliver us, and purge away our sins, for thy names sake.
theirs: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name: and deliver us, and purge away our sins, for thy name's sake.

ours: GIVE ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon ShoshannimEduth, A Psalm of Asaph.>> Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest [between] the cherubims, shine forth.

ours: SING aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, [A Psalm] of Asaph.>> Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.

ours: So I gave them up unto their own hearts lust: and they walked in their own counsels.
