theirs: So I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust: [and] they walked in their own counsels.

ours: GOD standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.

ours: KEEP not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm of Asaph.>> Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.

ours: Which perished at En-dor: they became as dung for the earth.
theirs: [Which] perished at Endor: they became [as] dung for the earth.

ours: HOW amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> How amiable [are] thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!

ours: LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.

ours: BOW down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I am poor and needy.
theirs: <<A Prayer of David.>> Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I [am] poor and needy.

ours: HIS foundation is in the holy mountains.
theirs: <<A Psalm [or] Song for the sons of Korah.>> His foundation [is] in the holy mountains.

ours: O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm for the sons of Korah, to the chief Musician upon Mahalath Leannoth, Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite.>> O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day [and] night before thee:

ours: I WILL sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.
theirs: <<Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite.>> I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.

ours: LORD, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.
theirs: <<A Prayer of Moses the man of God.>> Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

ours: IT is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:
theirs: <<A Psalm [or] Song for the sabbath day.>> [It is a] good [thing] to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:

ours: O SING unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
theirs: <<A Psalm.>> O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.

ours: The kings strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
theirs: The king's strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.

ours: MAKE a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.
theirs: <<A Psalm of praise.>> Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.

ours: I WILL sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.

ours: HEAR my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.
theirs: <<A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed, and poureth out his complaint before the LORD.>> Hear my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.

ours: BLESS the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, [bless] his holy name.

ours: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagles.
theirs: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good [things; so that] thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.

ours: But the mercy of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto childrens children;
theirs: But the mercy of the LORD [is] from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children's children;

ours: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth mans heart.
theirs: And wine [that] maketh glad the heart of man, [and] oil to make [his] face to shine, and bread [which] strengtheneth man's heart.

ours: Nevertheless he saved them for his names sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known.
theirs: Nevertheless he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known.

ours: They joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
theirs: They joined themselves also unto Baalpeor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.

ours: They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits end.
theirs: They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits' end.

ours: O GOD, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm of David.>> O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.

ours: HOLD not thy peace, O God of my praise;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise;

ours: But do thou for me, O GOD the Lord, for thy names sake: because thy mercy is good, deliver thou me.
theirs: But do thou for me, O GOD the Lord, for thy name's sake: because thy mercy [is] good, deliver thou me.

ours: THE LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

ours: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORDs name is to be praised.
theirs: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD's name [is] to be praised.

ours: NOT unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory, for thy mercy, and for thy truths sake.
theirs: Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory, for thy mercy, [and] for thy truth's sake.

ours: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of mens hands.
theirs: Their idols [are] silver and gold, the work of men's hands.

ours: The heaven, even the heavens, are the LORDs: but the earth hath he given to the children of men.
theirs: The heaven, [even] the heavens, [are] the LORD's: but the earth hath he given to the children of men.

ours: In the courts of the LORDs house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem. Praise ye the LORD.
theirs: In the courts of the LORD's house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem. Praise ye the LORD.

ours: This is the LORDs doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.
theirs: This is the LORD's doing; it [is] marvellous in our eyes.

ours: BLESSED are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.
theirs: ALEPH. Blessed [are] the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.

ours: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
theirs: BETH. Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed [thereto] according to thy word.

ours: Deal bountifully with thy servant, that I may live, and keep thy word.
theirs: GIMEL. Deal bountifully with thy servant, [that] I may live, and keep thy word.

ours: My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.
theirs: DALETH. My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.

ours: Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it unto the end.
theirs: HE. Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it [unto] the end.

ours: Let thy mercies come also unto me, O LORD, even thy salvation, according to thy word.
theirs: VAU. Let thy mercies come also unto me, O LORD, [even] thy salvation, according to thy word.

ours: Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.
theirs: ZAIN. Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.

ours: Thou art my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words.
theirs: CHETH. [Thou art] my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words.

ours: Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD, according unto thy word.
theirs: TETH. Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD, according unto thy word.

ours: Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.
theirs: JOD. Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.

ours: My soul fainteth for thy salvation: but I hope in thy word.
theirs: CAPH. My soul fainteth for thy salvation: [but] I hope in thy word.

ours: For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.
theirs: LAMED. For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.

ours: O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.
theirs: MEM. O how love I thy law! it [is] my meditation all the day.

ours: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
theirs: NUN. Thy word [is] a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

ours: I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.
theirs: SAMECH. I hate [vain] thoughts: but thy law do I love.

ours: I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.
theirs: AIN. I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.

ours: Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.
theirs: PE. Thy testimonies [are] wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.

ours: Righteous art thou, O LORD, and upright are thy judgments.
theirs: TZADDI. Righteous [art] thou, O LORD, and upright [are] thy judgments.

ours: I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes.
theirs: KOPH. I cried with [my] whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes.

ours: Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.
theirs: RESH. Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.

ours: Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.
theirs: SCHIN. Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.

ours: Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word.
theirs: TAU. Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word.

ours: IN my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> In my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.

ours: I WILL lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

ours: I WAS glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.

ours: For my brethren and companions sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee.
theirs: For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, Peace [be] within thee.

ours: UNTO thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.

ours: IF it had not been the LORD who was on our side, now may Israel say;
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> If [it had] not [been] the LORD who was on our side, now may Israel say;

ours: THEY that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> They that trust in the LORD [shall be] as mount Zion, [which] cannot be removed, [but] abideth for ever.

ours: WHEN the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.

ours: EXCEPT the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees for Solomon.>> Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh [but] in vain.

ours: BLESSED is every one that feareth the LORD; that walketh in his ways.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Blessed [is] every one that feareth the LORD; that walketh in his ways.

ours: Yea, thou shalt see thy childrens children, and peace upon Israel.
theirs: Yea, thou shalt see thy children's children, [and] peace upon Israel.

ours: MANY a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:

ours: OUT of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.

ours: LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.

ours: LORD, remember David, and all his afflictions:
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> LORD, remember David, [and] all his afflictions:

ours: For thy servant Davids sake turn not away the face of thine anointed.
theirs: For thy servant David's sake turn not away the face of thine anointed.

ours: BEHOLD, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> Behold, how good and how pleasant [it is] for brethren to dwell together in unity!

ours: It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aarons beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments;
theirs: [It is] like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, [even] Aaron's beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments;

ours: BEHOLD, bless ye the LORD, all ye servants of the LORD, which by night stand in the house of the LORD.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Behold, bless ye the LORD, all [ye] servants of the LORD, which by night stand in the house of the LORD.

ours: The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, the work of mens hands.
theirs: The idols of the heathen [are] silver and gold, the work of men's hands.

ours: How shall we sing the LORDs song in a strange land?
theirs: How shall we sing the LORD's song in a strange land?

ours: I WILL praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.

ours: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known [me].

ours: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mothers womb.
theirs: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother's womb.

ours: DELIVER me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Deliver me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;

ours: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders poison is under their lips. Selah.
theirs: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders' poison [is] under their lips. Selah.

ours: LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.

ours: Our bones are scattered at the graves mouth, as when one cutteth and cleaveth wood upon the earth.
theirs: Our bones are scattered at the grave's mouth, as when one cutteth and cleaveth [wood] upon the earth.

ours: I CRIED unto the LORD with my voice; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication.
theirs: <<Maschil of David; A Prayer when he was in the cave.>> I cried unto the LORD with my voice; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication.

ours: HEAR my prayer, O LORD, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> Hear my prayer, O LORD, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, [and] in thy righteousness.

ours: Quicken me, O LORD, for thy names sake: for thy righteousness sake bring my soul out of trouble.
theirs: Quicken me, O LORD, for thy name's sake: for thy righteousness' sake bring my soul out of trouble.

ours: BLESSED be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Blessed [be] the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, [and] my fingers to fight:

ours: I WILL extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.
theirs: <<David's [Psalm] of praise.>> I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.

ours: For I was my fathers son, tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother.
theirs: For I was my father's son, tender and only [beloved] in the sight of my mother.

ours: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers with thee.
theirs: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers' with thee.

ours: My son, keep thy fathers commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:
theirs: My son, keep thy father's commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

ours: So he that goeth in to his neighbours wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.
theirs: So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.

ours: The rich mans wealth is his strong city: the destruction of the poor is their poverty.
theirs: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city: the destruction of the poor [is] their poverty.

ours: As a jewel of gold in a swines snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.
theirs: [As] a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, [so is] a fair woman which is without discretion.

ours: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a mans hands shall be rendered unto him.
theirs: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of [his] mouth: and the recompence of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.

ours: A fools wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covereth shame.
theirs: A fool's wrath is presently known: but a prudent [man] covereth shame.

ours: A WISE son heareth his fathers instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.
theirs: A wise son [heareth] his father's instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.

ours: The ransom of a mans life are his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.
theirs: The ransom of a man's life [are] his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.

ours: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his childrens children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.
theirs: A good [man] leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner [is] laid up for the just.

ours: In the multitude of people is the kings honour: but in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.
theirs: In the multitude of people [is] the king's honour: but in the want of people [is] the destruction of the prince.

ours: The kings favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame.
theirs: The king's favour [is] toward a wise servant: but his wrath is [against] him that causeth shame.

ours: A fool despiseth his fathers instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.
theirs: A fool despiseth his father's instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.

ours: When a mans ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
theirs: When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

ours: A mans heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
theirs: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.

ours: A just weight and balance are the LORDs: all the weights of the bag are his work.
theirs: A just weight and balance [are] the LORD's: all the weights of the bag [are] his work.

ours: In the light of the kings countenance is life; and his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain.
theirs: In the light of the king's countenance [is] life; and his favour [is] as a cloud of the latter rain.

ours: Childrens children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.
theirs: Children's children [are] the crown of old men; and the glory of children [are] their fathers.

ours: The words of a mans mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook.
theirs: The words of a man's mouth [are as] deep waters, [and] the wellspring of wisdom [as] a flowing brook.

ours: A fools lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.
theirs: A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.

ours: A fools mouth is his destruction, and his lips are the snare of his soul.
theirs: A fool's mouth [is] his destruction, and his lips [are] the snare of his soul.

ours: The rich mans wealth is his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.
theirs: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.

ours: A mans gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
theirs: A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

ours: A mans belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; and with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.
theirs: A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; [and] with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.

ours: The kings wrath is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass.
theirs: The king's wrath [is] as the roaring of a lion; but his favour [is] as dew upon the grass.

ours: There are many devices in a mans heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
theirs: [There are] many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.

ours: Mans goings are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
theirs: Man's goings [are] of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?

ours: THE kings heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
theirs: The king's heart [is] in the hand of the LORD, [as] the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

ours: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbours house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
theirs: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and [so] hate thee.

ours: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fools back.
theirs: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.

ours: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fools wrath is heavier than them both.
theirs: A stone [is] heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath [is] heavier than them both.

ours: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a mans friend by hearty counsel.
theirs: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so [doth] the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.

ours: Thine own friend, and thy fathers friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brothers house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
theirs: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: [for] better [is] a neighbour [that is] near than a brother far off.

ours: And thou shalt have goats milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
theirs: And [thou shalt have] goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and [for] the maintenance for thy maidens.

ours: A mans pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
theirs: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.

ours: Many seek the rulers favour; but every mans judgment cometh from the LORD.
theirs: Many seek the ruler's favour; but [every] man's judgment [cometh] from the LORD.

ours: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his sons name, if thou canst tell?
theirs: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what [is] his name, and what [is] his son's name, if thou canst tell?

ours: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings palaces.
theirs: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.

ours: She is like the merchants ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
theirs: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

ours: The wise mans eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
theirs: The wise man's eyes [are] in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

ours: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fools voice is known by multitude of words.
theirs: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice [is known] by multitude of words.

ours: As he came forth of his mothers womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
theirs: As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

ours: A GOOD name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of ones birth.
theirs: A good name [is] better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

ours: WHO is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a mans wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
theirs: Who [is] as the wise [man]? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

ours: I counsel thee to keep the kings commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.
theirs: I [counsel thee] to keep the king's commandment, and [that] in regard of the oath of God.

ours: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise mans heart discerneth both time and judgment.
theirs: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.

ours: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor mans wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
theirs: Then said I, Wisdom [is] better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom [is] despised, and his words are not heard.

ours: A wise mans heart is at his right hand; but a fools heart at his left.
theirs: A wise man's heart [is] at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

ours: The words of a wise mans mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
theirs: The words of a wise man's mouth [are] gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

ours: THE song of songs, which is Solomons.
theirs: The song of songs, which [is] Solomon's.

ours: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mothers children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.
theirs: Look not upon me, because I [am] black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; [but] mine own vineyard have I not kept.

ours: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds tents.
theirs: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.

ours: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaohs chariots.
theirs: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.

ours: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.
theirs: My beloved [is] unto me [as] a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.

ours: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves eyes.
theirs: Behold, thou [art] fair, my love; behold, thou [art] fair; thou [hast] doves' eyes.

ours: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mothers house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
theirs: [It was] but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

ours: Behold his bed, which is Solomons; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
theirs: Behold his bed, which [is] Solomon's; threescore valiant men [are] about it, of the valiant of Israel.

ours: BEHOLD, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
theirs: Behold, thou [art] fair, my love; behold, thou [art] fair; thou [hast] doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair [is] as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

ours: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
theirs: Come with me from Lebanon, [my] spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

ours: I am my beloveds, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
theirs: I [am] my beloved's, and my beloved [is] mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

ours: HOW beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O princes daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
theirs: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs [are] like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

ours: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.
theirs: Thy neck [is] as a tower of ivory; thine eyes [like] the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose [is] as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

ours: I am my beloveds, and his desire is toward me.
theirs: I [am] my beloved's, and his desire [is] toward me.

ours: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mothers house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
theirs: I would lead thee, [and] bring thee into my mother's house, [who] would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

ours: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.
theirs: Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand [pieces] of silver.

ours: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his masters crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.
theirs: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: [but] Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

ours: And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORDs house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.
theirs: And it shall come to pass in the last days, [that] the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.

ours: Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind:
theirs: Whose arrows [are] sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind:

ours: Then said the LORD unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fullers field;
theirs: Then said the LORD unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shearjashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field;

ours: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliahs son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.
theirs: And the head of Ephraim [is] Samaria, and the head of Samaria [is] Remaliah's son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

ours: The LORD shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy fathers house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah; even the king of Assyria.
theirs: The LORD shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father's house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah; [even] the king of Assyria.

ours: MOREOVER the LORD said unto me, Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a mans pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
theirs: Moreover the LORD said unto me, Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man's pen concerning Mahershalalhashbaz.

ours: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
theirs: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz.

ours: Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliahs son;
theirs: Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son;

ours: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice den.
theirs: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice' den.

ours: Therefore shall all hands be faint, and every mans heart shall melt:
theirs: Therefore shall all hands be faint, and every man's heart shall melt:

ours: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
theirs: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

ours: Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpents root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent.
theirs: Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit [shall be] a fiery flying serpent.

ours: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the howling thereof unto Eglaim, and the howling thereof unto Beer-elim.
theirs: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the howling thereof unto Eglaim, and the howling thereof unto Beerelim.

ours: Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir-hareseth shall ye mourn; surely they are stricken.
theirs: Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kirhareseth shall ye mourn; surely [they are] stricken.

ours: Wherefore my bowels shall sound like an harp for Moab, and mine inward parts for Kir-haresh.
theirs: Wherefore my bowels shall sound like an harp for Moab, and mine inward parts for Kirharesh.

ours: He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lords house.
theirs: He will surely violently turn and toss thee [like] a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory [shall be] the shame of thy lord's house.

ours: And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his fathers house.
theirs: And I will fasten him [as] a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father's house.

ours: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his fathers house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups, even to all the vessels of flagons.
theirs: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups, even to all the vessels of flagons.

ours: Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potters clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?
theirs: Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?

ours: And he shall break it as the breaking of the potters vessel that is broken in pieces; he shall not spare: so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withal out of the pit.
theirs: And he shall break it as the breaking of the potters' vessel that is broken in pieces; he shall not spare: so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water [withal] out of the pit.

ours: For it is the day of the LORDs vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.
theirs: For [it is] the day of the LORD's vengeance, [and] the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.

ours: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fullers field.
theirs: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field.

ours: Then came forth unto him Eliakim, Hilkiahs son, which was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaphs son, the recorder.
theirs: Then came forth unto him Eliakim, Hilkiah's son, which was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaph's son, the recorder.

ours: How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my masters servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
theirs: How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master's servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

ours: Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall.
theirs: Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand [it]: and speak not to us in the Jews' language, in the ears of the people that [are] on the wall.

ours: Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews language, and said, Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.
theirs: Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language, and said, Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.

ours: But they held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the kings commandment was, saying, Answer him not.
theirs: But they held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the king's commandment was, saying, Answer him not.

ours: And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of mens hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them.
theirs: And have cast their gods into the fire: for they [were] no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them.

ours: For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant Davids sake.
theirs: For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake.

ours: And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Armenia: and Esar-haddon his son reigned in his stead.
theirs: And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Armenia: and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.

ours: Mine age is departed, and is removed from me as a shepherds tent: I have cut off like a weaver my life: he will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.
theirs: Mine age is departed, and is removed from me as a shepherd's tent: I have cut off like a weaver my life: he will cut me off with pining sickness: from day [even] to night wilt thou make an end of me.

ours: AT that time Merodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.
theirs: At that time Merodachbaladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.

ours: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORDs hand double for all her sins.
theirs: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD's hand double for all her sins.

ours: Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger that I sent? who is blind as he that is perfect, and blind as the LORDs servant?
theirs: Who [is] blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger [that] I sent? who [is] blind as [he that is] perfect, and blind as the LORD's servant?

ours: The LORD is well pleased for his righteousness sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.
theirs: The LORD is well pleased for his righteousness' sake; he will magnify the law, and make [it] honourable.

ours: One shall say, I am the LORDs; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel.
theirs: One shall say, I [am] the LORD's; and another shall call [himself] by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe [with] his hand unto the LORD, and surname [himself] by the name of Israel.

ours: For Jacob my servants sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.
theirs: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.

ours: For my names sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off.
theirs: For my name's sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off.

ours: THUS saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mothers divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away.
theirs: Thus saith the LORD, Where [is] the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors [is it] to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away.

ours: BEHOLD, the LORDs hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear:
theirs: Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear:

ours: They hatch cockatrice eggs, and weave the spiders web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.
theirs: They hatch cockatrice' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.

ours: As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seeds seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever.
theirs: As for me, this [is] my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that [is] upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever.

ours: FOR Zions sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalems sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth.
theirs: For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp [that] burneth.

ours: Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi-bah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.
theirs: Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.

ours: O LORD, why hast thou made us to err from thy ways, and hardened our heart from thy fear? Return for thy servants sake, the tribes of thine inheritance.
theirs: O LORD, why hast thou made us to err from thy ways, [and] hardened our heart from thy fear? Return for thy servants' sake, the tribes of thine inheritance.

ours: Which remain among the graves, and lodge in the monuments, which eat swines flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
theirs: Which remain among the graves, and lodge in the monuments, which eat swine's flesh, and broth of abominable [things is in] their vessels;

ours: Thus saith the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants sakes, that I may not destroy them all.
theirs: Thus saith the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and [one] saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing [is] in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all.

ours: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpents meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD.
theirs: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust [shall be] the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD.

ours: He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dogs neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swines blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol. Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations.
theirs: He that killeth an ox [is as if] he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, [as if] he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, [as if he offered] swine's blood; he that burneth incense, [as if] he blessed an idol. Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations.

ours: Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word; Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my names sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed.
theirs: Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word; Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed.

ours: They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swines flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD.
theirs: They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one [tree] in the midst, eating swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD.

ours: Wherefore I will yet plead with you, saith the LORD, and with your childrens children will I plead.
theirs: Wherefore I will yet plead with you, saith the LORD, and with your children's children will I plead.

ours: THEY say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another mans, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the LORD.
theirs: They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the LORD.

ours: Therefore the showers have been withholden, and there hath been no latter rain; and thou hadst a whores forehead, thou refusedst to be ashamed.
theirs: Therefore the showers have been withholden, and there hath been no latter rain; and thou hadst a whore's forehead, thou refusedst to be ashamed.

ours: How shall I pardon thee for this? thy children have forsaken me, and sworn by them that are no gods: when I had fed them to the full, they then committed adultery, and assembled themselves by troops in the harlots houses.
theirs: How shall I pardon thee for this? thy children have forsaken me, and sworn by [them that are] no gods: when I had fed them to the full, they then committed adultery, and assembled themselves by troops in the harlots' houses.

ours: They were as fed horses in the morning: every one neighed after his neighbours wife.
theirs: They were [as] fed horses in the morning: every one neighed after his neighbour's wife.

ours: Go ye up upon her walls, and destroy; but make not a full end: take away her battlements; for they are not the LORDs.
theirs: Go ye up upon her walls, and destroy; but make not a full end: take away her battlements; for they [are] not the LORD's.

ours: O YE children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Beth-haccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction.
theirs: O ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Bethhaccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction.

ours: Stand in the gate of the LORDs house, and proclaim there this word, and say, Hear the word of the LORD, all ye of Judah, that enter in at these gates to worship the LORD.
theirs: Stand in the gate of the LORD's house, and proclaim there this word, and say, Hear the word of the LORD, all [ye of] Judah, that enter in at these gates to worship the LORD.

ours: Then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit upon Davids throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.
theirs: Then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit upon David's throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.

ours: But if ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for your pride; and mine eye shall weep sore, and run down with tears, because the LORDs flock is carried away captive.
theirs: But if ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for [your] pride; and mine eye shall weep sore, and run down with tears, because the LORD's flock is carried away captive.

ours: O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy names sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.
theirs: O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou [it] for thy name's sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.

ours: Do not abhor us, for thy names sake, do not disgrace the throne of thy glory: remember, break not thy covenant with us.
theirs: Do not abhor [us], for thy name's sake, do not disgrace the throne of thy glory: remember, break not thy covenant with us.

ours: Arise, and go down to the potters house, and there I will cause thee to hear my words.
theirs: Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will cause thee to hear my words.

theirs: Then I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the wheels.

ours: O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potters hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.
theirs: O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay [is] in the potter's hand, so [are] ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.

ours: THUS saith the LORD, Go and get a potters earthen bottle, and take of the ancients of the people, and of the ancients of the priests;
theirs: Thus saith the LORD, Go and get a potter's earthen bottle, and [take] of the ancients of the people, and of the ancients of the priests;

ours: And shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Even so will I break this people and this city, as one breaketh a potters vessel, that cannot be made whole again: and they shall bury them in Tophet, till there be no place to bury.
theirs: And shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Even so will I break this people and this city, as [one] breaketh a potter's vessel, that cannot be made whole again: and they shall bury [them] in Tophet, till [there be] no place to bury.

theirs: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Pashur brought forth Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then said Jeremiah unto him, The LORD hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magormissabib.

ours: For thus saith the LORD unto the kings house of Judah; Thou art Gilead unto me, and the head of Lebanon: yet surely I will make thee a wilderness, and cities which are not inhabited.
theirs: For thus saith the LORD unto the king's house of Judah; Thou [art] Gilead unto me, [and] the head of Lebanon: [yet] surely I will make thee a wilderness, [and] cities [which] are not inhabited.

theirs: Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; [that] useth his neighbour's service without wages, and giveth him not for his work;

ours: And the burden of the LORD shall ye mention no more: for every mans word shall be his burden; for ye have perverted the words of the living God, of the LORD of hosts our God.
theirs: And the burden of the LORD shall ye mention no more: for every man's word shall be his burden; for ye have perverted the words of the living God, of the LORD of hosts our God.

theirs: Then took I the cup at the LORD's hand, and made all the nations to drink, unto whom the LORD had sent me:

ours: And there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the LORD, Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjath-jearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah:
theirs: And there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the LORD, Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah:

ours: And all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his sons son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.
theirs: And all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son's son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.

ours: Also I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Thus saith the LORD; Hearken not to the words of your prophets that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the LORDs house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you.
theirs: Also I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Thus saith the LORD; Hearken not to the words of your prophets that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the LORD's house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you.

ours: Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the LORDs house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place, and carried them to Babylon:
theirs: Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the LORD's house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place, and carried them to Babylon:

ours: Even the prophet Jeremiah said, Amen: the LORD do so: the LORD perform thy words which thou hast prophesied, to bring again the vessels of the LORDs house, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon into this place.
theirs: Even the prophet Jeremiah said, Amen: the LORD do so: the LORD perform thy words which thou hast prophesied, to bring again the vessels of the LORD's house, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon into this place.

ours: Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiahs neck, and brake it.
theirs: Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah's neck, and brake it.

ours: Because they have committed villany in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbours wives, and have spoken lying words in my name, which I have not commanded them; even I know, and am a witness, saith the LORD.
theirs: Because they have committed villany in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbours' wives, and have spoken lying words in my name, which I have not commanded them; even I know, and [am] a witness, saith the LORD.

ours: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacobs trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.
theirs: Alas! for that day [is] great, so that none [is] like it: it [is] even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.

ours: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacobs tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.
theirs: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob's tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.

ours: In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the childrens teeth are set on edge.
theirs: In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge.

ours: For then the king of Babylons army besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judahs house.
theirs: For then the king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which [was] in the king of Judah's house.

ours: So Hanameel mine uncles son came to me in the court of the prison according to the word of the LORD, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth, which is in the country of Benjamin: for the right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine; buy it for thyself. Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
theirs: So Hanameel mine uncle's son came to me in the court of the prison according to the word of the LORD, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that [is] in Anathoth, which [is] in the country of Benjamin: for the right of inheritance [is] thine, and the redemption [is] thine; buy [it] for thyself. Then I knew that this [was] the word of the LORD.

ours: And I bought the field of Hanameel my uncles son, that was in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, even seventeen shekels of silver.
theirs: And I bought the field of Hanameel my uncle's son, that [was] in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, [even] seventeen shekels of silver.

ours: And I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the sight of Hanameel mine uncles son, and in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison.
theirs: And I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the sight of Hanameel mine uncle's [son], and in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison.

ours: When the king of Babylons army fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish, and against Azekah: for these defenced cities remained of the cities of Judah.
theirs: When the king of Babylon's army fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish, and against Azekah: for these defenced cities remained of the cities of Judah.

ours: And Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes will I give into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life, and into the hand of the king of Babylons army, which are gone up from you.
theirs: And Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes will I give into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life, and into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, which are gone up from you.

ours: The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their fathers commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me.
theirs: The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me.

ours: Therefore go thou, and read in the roll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the LORD in the ears of the people in the LORDs house upon the fasting day: and also thou shalt read them in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities.
theirs: Therefore go thou, and read in the roll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the LORD in the ears of the people in the LORD's house upon the fasting day: and also thou shalt read them in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities.

ours: And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the LORD in the LORDs house.
theirs: And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the LORD in the LORD's house.

ours: Then read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the LORDs house, in the ears of all the people.
theirs: Then read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the LORD's house, in the ears of all the people.

ours: Then he went down into the kings house, into the scribes chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there, even Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
theirs: Then he went down into the king's house, into the scribe's chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there, [even] Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.

ours: So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll: and he took it out of Elishama the scribes chamber. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king.
theirs: So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll: and he took it out of Elishama the scribe's chamber. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king.

ours: Then Pharaohs army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem.
theirs: Then Pharaoh's army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem.

theirs: Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel; Thus shall ye say to the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to inquire of me; Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land.

ours: Then Zedekiah the king commanded that they should commit Jeremiah into the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread out of the bakers street, until all the bread in the city were spent. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.

theirs: Thus saith the LORD, This city shall surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, which shall take it.

theirs: Then the king commanded Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.

ours: So Ebed-melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.

ours: Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylons princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:
theirs: Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:

ours: But if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylons princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.
theirs: But if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon's princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.

ours: And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judahs house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylons princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back.
theirs: And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah's house [shall be] brought forth to the king of Babylon's princes, and those [women] shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, [and] they are turned away back.

ours: Then thou shalt say unto them, I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathans house, to die there.
theirs: Then thou shalt say unto them, I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathan's house, to die there.

ours: And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon.
theirs: And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, [even] Nergalsharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon.

ours: And it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the kings garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain.
theirs: And it came to pass, [that] when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain.

ours: But the Chaldeans army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him.
theirs: But the Chaldeans' army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him.

theirs: Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained.

ours: But Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
theirs: But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.

ours: THE word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after that Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all that were carried away captive of Jerusalem and Judah, which were carried away captive unto Babylon.

ours: Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the kings daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites.
theirs: Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that [were] in Mizpah, [even] the king's daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites.

ours: And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Beth-lehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
theirs: And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem, to go to enter into Egypt,

ours: Even men, and women, and children, and the kings daughters, and every person that Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.
theirs: [Even] men, and women, and children, and the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.

theirs: He shall break also the images of Bethshemesh, that [is] in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of the Egyptians shall he burn with fire.

ours: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
theirs: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give Pharaohhophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.

theirs: Therefore mine heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and mine heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kirheres: because the riches [that] he hath gotten are perished.
