ours: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
theirs: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.

ours: AND when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus band.
theirs: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto [one] named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

ours: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any mans life among you, but of the ship.
theirs: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of [any man's] life among you, but of the ship.

ours: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
theirs: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

ours: And the soldiers counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
theirs: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

ours: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
theirs: But when the Jews spake against [it], I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

ours: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
theirs: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

ours: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Saras womb:
theirs: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sara's womb:

ours: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adams transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.
theirs: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.

ours: For if by one mans offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)
theirs: For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)

ours: For as by one mans disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.
theirs: For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.

ours: Who shall lay any thing to the charge of Gods elect? It is God that justifieth.
theirs: Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? [It is] God that justifieth.

ours: BRETHREN, my hearts desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.
theirs: Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.

ours: For they being ignorant of Gods righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.
theirs: For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.

ours: As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers sakes.
theirs: As concerning the gospel, [they are] enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, [they are] beloved for the fathers' sakes.

ours: For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are Gods ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.
theirs: For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.

ours: Who art thou that judgest another mans servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.
theirs: Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

ours: For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lords.
theirs: For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's.

ours: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brothers way.
theirs: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in [his] brother's way.

ours: Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another mans foundation:
theirs: Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man's foundation:

ours: Now I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christs sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me;
theirs: Now I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christ's sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in [your] prayers to God for me;

ours: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judæa; and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;
theirs: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judaea; and that my service which [I have] for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;

ours: Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epænetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.
theirs: Likewise [greet] the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.

ours: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus household.
theirs: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus' [household].

ours: To God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
theirs: To God only wise, [be] glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen. <<[Written to the Romans from Corinthus, [and sent] by Phebe servant of the church at Cenchrea.]>>

ours: And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of mans wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:
theirs: And my speech and my preaching [was] not with enticing words of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:

ours: Which things also we speak, not in the words which mans wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
theirs: Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

ours: For we are labourers together with God: ye are Gods husbandry, ye are Gods building.
theirs: For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, [ye are] God's building.

ours: Every mans work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every mans work of what sort it is.
theirs: Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.

ours: If any mans work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.
theirs: If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.

ours: If any mans work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.
theirs: If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

ours: And ye are Christs; and Christ is Gods.
theirs: And ye are Christ's; and Christ [is] God's.

ours: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of mans judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self.
theirs: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man's judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self.

ours: We are fools for Christs sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised.
theirs: We [are] fools for Christ's sake, but ye [are] wise in Christ; we [are] weak, but ye [are] strong; ye [are] honourable, but we [are] despised.

ours: IT is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his fathers wife.
theirs: It is reported commonly [that there is] fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife.

ours: For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are Gods.
theirs: For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.

ours: For he that is called in the Lord, being a servant, is the Lords freeman: likewise also he that is called, being free, is Christs servant.
theirs: For he that is called in the Lord, [being] a servant, is the Lord's freeman: likewise also he that is called, [being] free, is Christ's servant.

ours: For if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idols temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;
theirs: For if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idol's temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;

ours: And this I do for the gospels sake, that I might be partaker thereof with you.
theirs: And this I do for the gospel's sake, that I might be partaker thereof with [you].

ours: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lords table, and of the table of devils.
theirs: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lord's table, and of the table of devils.

ours: Let no man seek his own, but every man anothers wealth.
theirs: Let no man seek his own, but every man another's [wealth].

ours: For the earth is the Lords, and the fulness thereof.
theirs: For the earth [is] the Lord's, and the fulness thereof.

ours: But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lords, and the fulness thereof:
theirs: But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth [is] the Lord's, and the fulness thereof:

ours: Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another mans conscience?
theirs: Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another [man's] conscience?

ours: When ye come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lords supper.
theirs: When ye come together therefore into one place, [this] is not to eat the Lord's supper.

ours: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lords death till he come.
theirs: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord's death till he come.

ours: For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lords body.
theirs: For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord's body.

ours: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christs at his coming.
theirs: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.

ours: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maran-atha.
theirs: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.

ours: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
theirs: My love [be] with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi by Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, and Timotheus.]>>

ours: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judæa.
theirs: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.

ours: Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christs gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,
theirs: Furthermore, when I came to Troas to [preach] Christ's gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,

ours: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every mans conscience in the sight of God.
theirs: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.

ours: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus sake.
theirs: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.

ours: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.
theirs: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

ours: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christs stead, be ye reconciled to God.
theirs: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech [you] by us: we pray [you] in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.

ours: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christs, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christs, even so are we Christs.
theirs: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he [is] Christ's, even so [are] we Christ's.

ours: Not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other mens labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly,
theirs: Not boasting of things without [our] measure, [that is], of other men's labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly,

ours: To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another mans line of things made ready to our hand.
theirs: To preach the gospel in the [regions] beyond you, [and] not to boast in another man's line of things made ready to our hand.

ours: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christs sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
theirs: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

ours: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi, [a city] of Macedonia, by Titus and Lucas.]>>

ours: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
theirs: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:

ours: And profited in the Jews religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
theirs: And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.

ours: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mothers womb, and called me by his grace,
theirs: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called [me] by his grace,

ours: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lords brother.
theirs: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.

ours: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judæa which were in Christ:
theirs: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:

ours: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no mans person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
theirs: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man's person:) for they who seemed [to be somewhat] in conference added nothing to me:

ours: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though it be but a mans covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.
theirs: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though [it be] but a man's covenant, yet [if it be] confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.

ours: And if ye be Christs, then are ye Abrahams seed, and heirs according to the promise.
theirs: And if ye [be] Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

ours: And they that are Christs have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.
theirs: And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.

ours: Bear ye one anothers burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
theirs: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

ours: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
theirs: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen. <<[Unto the Galatians written from Rome.]>>

ours: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christs sake hath forgiven you.
theirs: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.

ours: Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.
theirs: Grace [be] with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen. <<[Written from Rome unto the Ephesians by Tychicus.]>>

ours: For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christs.
theirs: For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's.

ours: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Cæsars household.
theirs: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<[It was written to the Philippians from Rome by Epaphroditus.]>>

ours: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his bodys sake, which is the church:
theirs: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body's sake, which is the church:

ours: For which things sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:
theirs: For which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:

ours: Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sisters son to Barnabas, (touching whom ye received commandments: if he come unto you, receive him;)
theirs: Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister's son to Barnabas, (touching whom ye received commandments: if he come unto you, receive him;)

ours: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
theirs: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace [be] with you. Amen. <<[Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.]>>

ours: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judæa are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews:
theirs: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they [have] of the Jews:

ours: And to esteem them very highly in love for their works sake. And be at peace among yourselves.
theirs: And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. [And] be at peace among yourselves.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] unto the Thessalonians was written from Athens.]>>

ours: Neither did we eat any mans bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:
theirs: Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Thessalonians was written from Athens.]>>

ours: Of whom is Hymenæus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
theirs: Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

ours: But refuse profane and old wives fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness.
theirs: But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself [rather] unto godliness.

ours: Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.
theirs: Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.

ours: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other mens sins: keep thyself pure.
theirs: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.

ours: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomachs sake and thine often infirmities.
theirs: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities.

ours: Some mens sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after.
theirs: Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some [men] they follow after.

ours: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.
theirs: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace [be] with thee. Amen. <<[The first to Timothy was written from Laodicea, which is the chiefest city of Phrygia Pacatiana.]>>

ours: Therefore I endure all things for the elects sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
theirs: Therefore I endure all things for the elect's sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.

ours: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenæus and Philetus;
theirs: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;

ours: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the masters use, and prepared unto every good work.
theirs: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, [and] prepared unto every good work.

ours: The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
theirs: The Lord Jesus Christ [be] with thy spirit. Grace [be] with you. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] unto Timotheus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Ephesians, was written from Rome, when Paul was brought before Nero the second time.]>>

ours: PAUL, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of Gods elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;
theirs: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;

ours: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucres sake.
theirs: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.

ours: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
theirs: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace [be] with you all. Amen. <<[It was written to Titus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Cretians, from Nicopolis of Macedonia.]>>

ours: Yet for loves sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
theirs: Yet for love's sake I rather beseech [thee], being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen. <<[Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a servant.]>>

ours: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the peoples: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
theirs: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.

ours: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aarons rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
theirs: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein [was] the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;

ours: He that despised Moses law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:
theirs: He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

ours: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the kings commandment.
theirs: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw [he was] a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.

ours: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaohs daughter;
theirs: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;

ours: Grace be with you all. Amen.
theirs: Grace [be] with you all. Amen. <<[Written to the Hebrews from Italy by Timothy.]>>

ours: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this mans religion is vain.
theirs: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion [is] vain.

ours: Behold, we put bits in the horses mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
theirs: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.

ours: And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every mans work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear:
theirs: And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning [here] in fear:

ours: Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lords sake: whether it be to the king, as supreme;
theirs: Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord's sake: whether it be to the king, as supreme;

ours: But and if ye suffer for righteousness sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;
theirs: But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy [are ye]: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;

ours: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christs sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.
theirs: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ's sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.

ours: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other mens matters.
theirs: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or [as] a thief, or [as] an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men's matters.

ours: Neither as being lords over Gods heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.
theirs: Neither as being lords over [God's] heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.

ours: But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with mans voice forbad the madness of the prophet.
theirs: But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet.

ours: I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his names sake.
theirs: I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake.

ours: Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: but he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also.
theirs: Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: [(but) he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also].

ours: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brothers righteous.
theirs: Not as Cain, [who] was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.

ours: But whoso hath this worlds good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?
theirs: But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels [of compassion] from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?

ours: For the truths sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever.
theirs: For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever.

ours: Because that for his names sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
theirs: Because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.

ours: These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having mens persons in admiration because of advantage.
theirs: These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling [words], having men's persons in admiration because of advantage.

ours: I was in the Spirit on the Lords day, and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,
theirs: I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,

ours: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my names sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.
theirs: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.

ours: I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satans seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth.
theirs: I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, [even] where Satan's seat [is]: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas [was] my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth.

ours: And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angels hand.
theirs: And the smoke of the incense, [which came] with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel's hand.

ours: And I took the little book out of the angels hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter.
theirs: And I took the little book out of the angel's hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter.

ours: AND I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Fathers name written in their foreheads.
theirs: And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty [and] four thousand, having his Father's name written in their foreheads.

ours: And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lambs wife.
theirs: And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.

ours: And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lambs book of life.
theirs: And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither [whatsoever] worketh abomination, or [maketh] a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<THE END.>>
